macro.text: Nasdaq-100 futures −1.9%, S&P 500 −1%, Dow −0.4% after all three fell more than 2% Thursday; VIX near 31, highest since March. Anthropic (ANT) −6 to −9% premarket after a +17% debut (I'm built by Anthropic).
Asia AI chip rout: Taiex −6.2% (−17.5% week, worst since 1991), Kospi −5.2%, Nikkei −5.1%, SoftBank −14.5%; ASML −5.8% in Europe.
Bonds rally: 10-year 4.99% (−6 bp), 2-year 4.71% (−6 bp), 30-year 5.36%. A December 9 hike is still fully priced; Waller (wants 50 bp or a signalled January hike) speaks today.
Oil steady to lower: WTI 81.86 (−0.7%), Brent 88.75 (−0.8%). NYT says Trump is weighing fresh Iran strikes, no decision; rising U.S. inventories cap prices.
Havens sold too: gold −2.9% to 3,579 (−8.9% this week, a 52-week low in futures); dollar index 103.66 (−0.2%).

briefs.read: Risk-off: QQQ −1.7%, SPY −0.9% premarket after Thursday's 2% drop; VIX 30.76, highest since March. Chips lead the selling (SMH −3.2%) after Taiwan's worst week since 1991; Intuit's guide cut hits software, while staples and utilities get money. No U.S. red event; Waller speaks, UMich at 10:00. The 9:30 bar was the high two days running: wait for 10:15 before trusting a gap.

focus: Nasdaq-100 futures −1.9%, S&P −1% after Thursday's 2% drop; VIX 30.76, highest since March
Asia chip rout: Taiex −6.2% (worst week since 1991); AMD −6.4%, TSM −5.7%, MU −4.9%
Intuit −9.4%: Q1 beat but FY27 revenue guide cut, Mailchimp sold; PLTR −4.2% in sympathy
Anthropic (ANT) −6 to −9% premarket after a +17% debut (I'm built by Anthropic)
Money into staples (XLP +1.2%), utilities, health care; 10-year back under 5% (4.99%)
Ross −5.8% (light holiday guide), Elastic −3.7%; Walmart +1.8%, Gap +3.5%
bigPicture: The market is selling the AI trade on every piece of news: the Anthropic debut was a sell-the-news event, and Asia's chip markets had their worst week in decades.
Beats are no longer enough: Intuit, Ross, Elastic and Keysight all beat and fell on outlook or sector. Only guide raises outside AI (Walmart, Gap) get bought.
Defensives win: staples, utilities and health care lead premarket as gold and the dollar also slip; it's a de-risking day, not a rotation into another growth theme.
Yields easing (10-year 4.99%) has not helped tech: a December hike stays fully priced and Waller wants 50 bp.
snapshot.takeaway: This is a high-VIX, gap-down Friday after two days where the 9:30 bar set the high. Gap-downs on real news (INTU, ROST, TSM) can keep going, but sympathy gaps can snap back hard: let 10:15 settle which it is before trusting any setup, and expect wide option spreads at the open.

Intuit's cut guide (−9.4%) and Elastic's soft revenue guide (−3.7%) feed the 'AI disrupts software' worry; IGV −2.6%. PLTR −4.2%, DDOG −3.0%, SNOW −2.8%, MSFT −2.5%; ANT fading after its debut adds supply pressure.
MSFT −2.5%, AMZN −2.5%, ORCL −3.4% (ORCL closed at its lowest since April 2024). The 10-year back under 5% helps the debt-funded builders a little, but a December hike is fully priced.
Keysight's record orders (+53%, book-to-bill 1.17) confirm AI networking demand, but it's −2.8% premarket with the chip tape; industrials (XLI −0.6%) are holding up better than chips.
WTI 81.86 (−0.7%), Brent 88.75 (−0.8%) even with the NYT report that Trump is weighing new Iran strikes; rising U.S. inventories cap prices. XLE −0.6%, −9.9% in a month.
XLP +1.2%, the top sector premarket, after −1.5% Thursday. Walmart +1.8% on three target raises; Costco +1.4%. Money hiding from tech, helped by lower yields.

bigNames.text: Rout deepened on a report that the SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting; longest weekly losing streak since 2008, per MarketWatch.
Broadcom fell on a report that Google cut its plans for Broadcom AI chips; AMD and Micron (about -12.7%) extended losses.
Anthropic's stock came within 5 cents of its $83 IPO price on day two, then bounced to close at $88.30. I'm built by Anthropic.
Trump threatened to ban U.S. firms from building AI data centres overseas: a new policy risk for the AI infrastructure trade.

briefs.read: Risk-off held, but SPY first filled its gap and topped at 10:00 (718.29) before breaking down at 10:20; it closed at the lows, 690.91 (-3.49%), VIX 35.89. Morning setups: AMD, TSM and PLTR puts sides triggered (10:25-10:45); ROST and WMT calls sides worked early; INTU spiked to 300.44 then broke 273.05 at 15:50.
